messages:
Alex K: Quick decision needed: how should we handle burst credit expiry/rollover and accounting? Sales are getting pushback if credits expire too fast. We need a single policy for hosted + dedicated that legal + billing can operationalize.
Maria G: Key UX goals: predictable cost, simple buy flow, and visible balance. Options: 1) monthly non-rollover credits (burn-this-month), 2) annual rollover up to X%, 3) credits that convert to a discounted overage price if unused.
Jamal R: Field feedback: most customers accept non-rollover for 'one-off emergency packs' but will ask for rollover on committed burst allocations bundled in enterprise deals. Distinguish "purchased one-off" vs "bundled committed".
Sara L: Legal implications: rollover creates future liability on our books and changes revenue recognition. Need finance sign-off if we allow >90-day rollover. Also watch tax/VAT for prepaid credits in EU — need invoice-level granularity.
Lee N: Implementation: tracking balance per org + per-project is straightforward. Harder bits: synced usage across Dedicated and Private (on-prem) where we can't enforce server-side checks easily. For private deploy, recommend 'reporting-based' consumption with reconciliation invoices.
Nora T (Finance): From rev-rec perspective, prefer burn-to-recognize on redemption. If credits never expire, we might need to defer revenue. Practical compromise: set a max 12-month expiry for purchased credits.
Maria G: UX idea: show 'expires on' date and estimated runout at current usage. Allow admins to set project-level allocation.
Jamal R: Competitive ask: customers want ability to reallocate credits between projects without penalty. That should be an admin action in console.
Lee N: Flag design: `burst_credit.expiry_days`, `burst_credit.scope: org|project`, `burst_credit.transferable: true|false`. Default: expiry_days=90, scope=org, transferable=false.
Sara L: Transferable credits raise fraud/contract issues (reseller-like behavior). If we open transfers, need audit trail and optional approval workflow for enterprise.
Maria G: Pricing model differential: emergency single-buy = 2.2x committed unit price. Bundled committed burst = 1.1x unit price but with rollover and transferability. Also add volume tiers: >$250k annual => 15% off burst price.
BillingBot: Note: Stripe supports prepaid coupon-like products but for enterprise invoices we'll need metered line items + credit application logic. We'll need to map credit usage to invoice adjustments.
Nora T: Also confirm handling of refunds: if a customer returns unused prepaid credits within 30 days, allow pro-rata refund. After 30 days, credits are non-refundable. Add fraud exception clause.
Alex K: Launch criteria candidate list:
- Policy doc: expiry/rollover + transfer and refund rules published
- Billing: stripe + invoicing flow tested with applied credit adjustments (end-to-end)
- Console: balance, expiry date, transfer UI, admin logs
- Legal: contract addendum for bundled committed credits & private deploy reconciliation terms
- Finance: revenue recognition process documented for credits
- Infra: enforcement for hosted/dedicated; reconciliation path for private
- 2 pilot customers (one hosted, one dedicated) to validate UX and billing
Maria G: Flags for GA: default expiry 90 days, auto-topup off. Admin can enable `allow_transfers` for accounts with enterprise agreement.
Jamal R: Sales requirement: add a "one-time emergency buy" CTA in console with checkbox "apply credits immediately" + clear billing confirmation.
Lee N: Risk note: unlimited transferability + rollover increases our cost exposure. Any rollout should include rate-limits and an overage fallback (downgrade to lower-cost model or throttling).
Sara L: I'll draft contract text to cover: expiry, transfers, refunds, private deploy reconciliation, and emergency throttling notice.
Nora T: Finance asks for a list of projected credit sales for next 12 months to model deferred revenue. Lee, can you add a cost delta estimate for burst traffic patterns?
Lee N: Yes - I'll run 3 scenarios (low/med/high) and upload numbers. ETA 48 hours.
Alex K: Action items:
- Sara: contract redlines for credits (due Tue morning)
- Nora: revenue recognition memo + refund rules (due Tue afternoon)
- Lee: infra cost model & flag implementation plan (48h)
- Maria: UX flows + copy for emergency-buy + transfer modal (EOD tomorrow)
- Jamal: list top 10 customers asking for rollover/transfer so we can prioritize pilots
- BillingBot: start a ticket to confirm Stripe + invoice mapping for credits
ProductBot: Linked epic PRD-910 (Burst/Prepaid Credits): https://redwood.example/epics/PRD-910
Alex K: Ok meeting scheduled next Wed 9am PT to finalize policy. If anyone objects to the default expiry 90 days, raise now. :thumbsup:
